verdict.line: You lose if you let Yorick's Q sustain and Maiden drag the fight out; you win if you force a burst trade off your W-into-E combo before his R is up or while it's down.

brief.thesis: This matchup is a race between two self-sustaining melee kits, and the data confirms it's coin-flip close at 50.9% over 1324 games. Yorick's Q (Last Rites) heals him on landed empowered autos, which is exactly why OP.GG warns against prolonged melee combat — every extra second of brawling is a heal tick for him. Aatrox's actual edge is burst: W (Infernal Chains) forces a reposition into range-825 damage, and if he doesn't clear the zone he's dragged in and hit again, which is the setup for a short violent trade rather than a long one. Before level 6, Yorick has no Maiden to extend fights or split-push with, which is where Aatrox's solo-kill advantage actually lives.

theirWindow.when: Maiden summoned and W wall is up
theirWindow.what: Yorick's attacks against the Maiden's target deal bonus damage and the Maiden raises Walkers off anything that dies nearby, so a dragged-out fight here snowballs fast. Back off, let the Maiden's duration run down, or kill the Maiden itself before committing again.

yourWindow.when: His E and R are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Without Mourning Mist's armor shred/slow or Maiden backup, Yorick has only Q sustain to lean on. Land W to force the reposition, stack Q swings, and use E's passive heal-on-damage to win the short trade before he can reset.

powerCurve.note: Q sustain trades evenly with early pokes

start.why: Highest-winrate start in the matchup (50.1% over 1087 games) — the extra sustain and damage keep you even through early Q/E poke trades.

boots.why: Most-picked boots (78.1% pick, 50.5% WR) and it directly dulls Yorick's empowered-auto Q and his Maiden's attacks, both of which are basic-attack damage.

core.why: Burst and the shield proc reward the forced W-into-E trade pattern this matchup is built around.
On-hit burst plus healing lets your first-strike Q land harder and keeps you alive through his Q sustain race.
This path has the best winrate of the listed builds (61.2% over 98 games) — the damage-over-time conversion is what lets you walk away from a trade instead of dying to delayed poke.

situational.when: he starts building armor or you need more sustained DPS to beat his grave-dig healing in a longer siege
you need the extra dash/finishing burst to close out a short trade before his Maiden or Q heal can swing it back
the game goes long and you want ability haste to stack more W/E/Q resets through a teamfight
his E slow and any enemy CC are chaining you down and you need the tenacity more than the AA reduction

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the sustained-combat angle of this lane — it scales up through a trade and converts to healing, which matters because you're trying to out-sustain Yorick's Q, not just burst and leave.

summoners.why: Most-picked combo in the matchup (77.2% pick) and it directly undercuts the thing Yorick relies on most — Ignite's healing reduction cuts into his Q self-heal and his Maiden-fueled sustain right when you're trying to close out your solo-kill-favored burst window.

playing.title: Bait, don't brawl
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read is correct here: Yorick's Q heals him on landed empowered autos every 6-4s, so dragging a fight past your initial burst lets him out-heal it. Land your stacked Q swings and E-dash damage, then disengage instead of standing in extended melee.

playing.title: Hook him before he grave-digs
playing.detail: W (Infernal Chains, range 825) damages the first enemy hit and drags him to the center if he doesn't clear the impact zone fast — land it before he can Q for his heal, turning what would be a slow trade into a forced burst.

playing.title: Kill the Maiden, not just Yorick
playing.detail: Once his R is up, his attacks against the Maiden's target deal bonus damage and she raises Walkers off anything that dies nearby. If he ults mid-fight, prioritize the Maiden pet itself before continuing to trade.

playing.title: Time Deathbringer with your dash
playing.detail: Your passive next-attack proc is periodic, not always up — watch for the Deathbringer Stance ready indicator and line it up with E's dash-and-heal-on-damage so one combo covers both your burst and your sustain.

playing.title: Expect armor loss after his E lands
playing.detail: Mourning Mist (cooldown 12-8s) reduces armor, slows, and marks on hit, so auto trades hurt more right after it connects. Use your own E to reposition out of his range-700 throw instead of facetanking the follow-up.

playing.title: Force all-ins before level 6
playing.detail: Before Yorick has his Maiden, he has no tool to extend a fight or threaten a side lane. This is where your data-backed solo-kill edge actually applies — use your lower W/E cooldowns (20-12s and 9-5s respectively) to initiate repeatedly.

brief.patchCaveat: The build path, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample numbers above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why those choices work, the timing windows, and the trade pattern — is my own tactical read layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Do not fight Yorick in a prolonged melee combat. Use your skills whenever they come off cooldown to deal burst damage. Try to get rid of his (R) before fighting him.
